34 The diagram shows six identical resistors connected in a circuit.
Q
P
R
S
In which branch of the circuit is the most power dissipated?
A
PQ
B
QR
C
RS
D
SP

hints: Notice how many identical resistors are in each branch: PQ has two in series, QR has one, SP has one, and RS has two in parallel.
Recall power in a branch is $P = I^2R_{branch}$ where $I$ is the current through that branch, so compare the PQR route of $3R$ with the PSR route of $1.5R$ between P and R.
Work out the two route currents from the same p.d. across P and R, then compare $I^2$ times branch resistance for PQ, QR, RS and SP.
walkthrough: Identify the circuit between the battery terminals P and R. There are two parallel routes: route P-Q-R and route P-S-R.
Find each branch resistance with each resistor $R$: $R_{PQ}=2R$, $R_{QR}=R$, $R_{SP}=R$, and $R_{RS}=R/2$ for two in parallel.
Find each route resistance: $R_{PQR}=2R+R=3R$ and $R_{PSR}=R+R/2=1.5R$. With the same p.d. $V$ across P and R, current $I=V/R_{route}$, so the PSR current $I_2$ is twice the PQR current $I_1$.
Use $P=I^2R_{branch}$ for total power in a branch: $P_{PQ}=I_1^2(2R)$, $P_{QR}=I_1^2R$, $P_{SP}=I_2^2R$, $P_{RS}=I_2^2(R/2)$.
Substitute $I_2=2I_1$: $P_{SP}=4I_1^2R$, while $P_{PQ}=2I_1^2R$, $P_{RS}=2I_1^2R$ and $P_{QR}=I_1^2R$. Hence SP dissipates most. This is option D.

A.explanation: Branch PQ has resistance $2R$ but carries only the smaller PQR current $I_1$, so its power $I_1^2(2R)$ is less than in SP.

B.explanation: Branch QR has one resistor carrying the smaller PQR current $I_1$, so its power $I_1^2R$ is the smallest of the four branches.

C.explanation: Branch RS is $R/2$ from two resistors in parallel and carries the larger PSR current, but $I_2^2(R/2)$ is only half the power of SP.

D.explanation: Branch SP has one resistor carrying the full larger PSR current $I_2$, giving $I_2^2R$, which is the largest $I^2R$ value in the circuit.
